page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU instance featuring three dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Graphics acceleration is delivered via a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with a 0.5 allocation, providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside weaker multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1343.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1705.53, both placing in the average tier. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3293.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 5059.76, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 35.06 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 26.33 GB/sec.

This instance is designed for workloads requiring GPU acceleration with moderate compute requirements, such as small-scale machine learning inference, basic image processing, or lightweight graphics rendering. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server processed 549.08 tokens/sec for prompts and generated 125.03 tokens/sec using a small 135M model, though performance dropped to 4.56 tokens/sec for text generation with a medium 7B model. The fractional GPU allocation offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks that do not require a full dedicated card, balancing memory capacity against lower multi-core CPU throughput.
